findings.title: No test that non-matching sessions still flush when fallbacks are set
findings.why_it_matters: The only new test covers the fallback-match path. The new else branch (hash matches neither the current secret nor any fallback, so flush and anonymous) is never run with SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS non-empty, and neither is the missing-session-hash case. A regression that made the fallback check too permissive, such as dropping the `session_hash and` guard or mis-handling `any(...)`, would let a stale or tampered session authenticate or raise TypeError. The new test would still pass. The existing invalidation tests all run with empty fallbacks, so the loop is a no-op there. Adding a case with a non-matching fallback, and one with the hash removed, would pin this security-relevant behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tests to TestGetUser. (1) Log in, then change the user's password and call get_user under override_settings(SECRET_KEY='newsecret', SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS=['unrelated-old-secret']); assert AnonymousUser is returned and the session was flushed (session_key changed or empty). (2) Log in, delete request.session[HASH_SESSION_KEY], and call get_user with SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS set; assert AnonymousUser and no exception.
evidence: tests/auth_tests/test_basic.py:144-165 -- only test_get_user_fallback_secret, which has a matching fallback; grep of tests/ shows no other test combining SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS with get_user or HASH_SESSION_KEY

residual_risks: Fallback verification calls user.get_session_auth_fallback_hash(), which only exists on AbstractBaseUser. A custom user model that duck-types or overrides get_session_auth_hash() would get AttributeError, or have its override ignored on the fallback path, when the hash fails to verify. No test covers it. Only checked by reading the diff; not run.
testing_gaps: get_session_auth_fallback_hash() is not tested directly: the multi-fallback order and the empty-fallbacks case (generator yields nothing) are covered only indirectly through the single-fallback get_user test.

The new test does not check that cycle_key keeps the session data and that the session store holds the rewritten hash. It does check this indirectly, since the second get_user call with only the new secret returns a User.
